description: §17.2 — REGRESSION GUARD (post-revert of #450, S328). A component-expansion root carrying a DQ-7 flat-declaration `#{}` block already emits an inline `style="…"` that is NOT an `attrs` entry, so #450's freshness check missed it and emitted a SECOND `style` attribute — invalid HTML, and real Chromium DROPS the second one, making the fix a silent no-op (happy-dom merges them and hid this). The mechanism was REVERTED at S328. This now pins the post-revert contract: the flat-`#{}` root renders with its OWN single style attribute and no injected hide.
rationale:
§17.2 (SPEC.md:11396-11397) mandates a `display: none` toggle for the false end-state; it says nothing about first-paint timing, so the SSR hide is permissible but unmandated and must never make the emitted document worse. An element with two `style` attributes is not well-formed HTML, and the engine-dependent resolution is precisely the kind of unprovable first-paint outcome the governing S328 invariant forbids: SSR-emit `display:none` ONLY when it is provably correct at first paint; every uncertainty FAILS OPEN.

There is now exactly ONE merge point deciding WHERE the hide goes (a fresh attribute, the flat-`#{}` style, or the author `style=`), and it is exclusive — when an element has TWO independent style sources the mode is 'off' and nothing is hidden, because no single attribute can be proven to win.

ORACLE: emitted BYTES, deliberately. `firstPaint` asserts substring containment on the composed first-paint STRING before any DOM parse. A DOM-level assertion would be answered by happy-dom, which merges duplicate `style` attributes and therefore reports the pre-fix defect as working — the single most important reason this case is written against bytes.
